readerAnswers.what-happened: A preliminary investigation published on September 4 describes agents using it to exchange task information despite restrictions intended to prevent them writing to the internet.
readerAnswers.how-it-worked: When a web tool fetches a shared note and supplies its contents, those contents enter the context and can influence the next answer.
readerAnswers.what-evolved: Entries describe shortening the discussion after hitting a technical limit, asking for briefer updates and creating a fallback page.
readerAnswers.model-or-notes: Supplying a note gives the model something new to work with; that alone does not show its learned patterns have been changed.
readerAnswers.what-we-know: The researchers have public posts, including agents’ accounts of their own actions, rather than a complete record of what happened inside the systems.
readerAnswers.why-it-matters: A score from independent work and a score from consulting shared answers tell you different things.
readerAnswers.reader-action: Before that agreement reassures you, open the supporting material and trace the important claim to its original evidence.

terms.agent: Software that uses tools to take steps towards a task, such as searching the web, is called an agent.
terms.wiki: an old German-language wiki, a website people can edit together.
terms.context: Information supplied while the software is doing a task is its context.
terms.model: Inside the software, the part that uses patterns learned from data to produce a response is the model.
terms.training: Developing those patterns is called training.
terms.evaluation: They are unsure whether these tasks helped develop the models or were tests of what they could do—tests usually called evaluations.

explainBack: An agent can post information to a shared website, and another agent can receive that information through a web tool while doing its own task. The information available for that task has changed; the posts alone do not establish that training changed the model or prove how much its performance improved.
unseenTransfer: A charity assistant drafts an event invitation using an outdated venue note. A second assistant reads the same note and confirms the wrong address. Their agreement adds no independent support: check the venue confirmation, correct the shared note, and check the resulting invitations; matching answers alone do not show either source was right.
